scope: Editorial revision only. Preserve source data, illustrative values, slide order and supplied Vopak master.

findings: Demand is concentrated
Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal and Western Cape account for 68.6% of reported 2022 petrol/diesel sales.
Four reporting regions
Eastern coast: EC/KZN. Inland: GP/FS/LP/MP/NW. Western coast: WC. Other: NC. Boundaries are reporting groups.
Sales locate the historical market
Colours show provincial sales totals, not demand density or customer catchments. Storage points show the infrastructure context.
3.action: Manish: refresh a complete year and reconcile the source flags. Nigel: confirm the customer markets to test against Durban and Lesedi.

findings: Gauteng remains the largest market
The reported series places Gauteng above the other provinces throughout 2013–2022. Volumes differ across the smaller markets.
The series stops at 2022
2022 is the latest complete year in this extract. Only Q1 is available for 2023, so it is excluded from annual comparisons.
Historical reconciliation is open
Provincial totals differ from national sales in six years: 2013, 2014, 2015, 2017, 2018 and 2021.
4.action: Manish: reconcile flagged workbook cells and source newer observed sales. Record revisions and incomplete periods before updating the outlook.

findings: Reported imports exceed exports
The government report gives 14.8 bn litres of petrol/diesel imports and 1.71 bn litres of exports in 2024. Figures are rounded.
Diesel imports need reconciliation
FIASA gives 14.793 bn litres of diesel imports versus 10.8 bn litres in the government report. The scope difference remains open.
Entry ports need product evidence
Liquid-bulk port cargo includes crude and other liquids. Product-specific records are needed to allocate petrol/diesel imports.
5.action: Manish: match trade, actual production and stock changes by product and year. Nigel: obtain product-specific port records.

findings: Darker means lower transport cost
Cells show example road cost from Durban or Lesedi. The rate is illustrative and excludes fuel price, storage and pipeline tariffs.
Grey means unassessed
Grey areas have no assessed road connection under this illustration. They are not confirmed to be inaccessible.
A cost surface is a first screen
Pipeline and rail lines are context. Route capacity, product compatibility and customer rights still determine serviceable demand.
9.action: Nigel: select the first customer destination and cost threshold. Manish: replace example rates with dated route costs and access evidence.

findings: Use one inland customer destination
Gauteng is the comparison point. Lesedi is Vopak’s inland facility. Competing gateways can serve customers without using Lesedi.
Matola is the eastern alternative
The N4/Maputo corridor approaches Gauteng from Mozambique. Fuel handling, border access and road/rail service need verification.
Walvis is a western comparator
The Trans-Kalahari corridor approaches Gauteng via Namibia and Botswana. This map does not establish an eastern-coast catchment.
10.action: Manish: compare each gateway for the same product, customer and period, including handling, transport and border costs. Nigel selects the customer.

findings: Count customer demand once
Example receipts of 2.8 at Durban and 2.0 at Lesedi include a shared 1.8 transfer. Unique demand served is therefore 3.0 bn litres.
Reach does not establish capture
The example accessible volume is 8.5, including the current 3.0. The additional 5.5 requires physical and commercial evidence.
Examples are separate from sales
These market volumes illustrate the calculation. They are not the reported 2022 regional totals or actual Vopak deliveries.
11.action: Nigel: request customer deliveries, destinations and transfer records. Manish: calculate unique served demand before estimating additional access.

findings: Flows set the service requirement
Incremental customer flows determine receipt, dispatch and inventory needs. A national import gap alone does not size new storage.
Published tanks are a starting point
The inventory has mixed capacity bases and incomplete coverage. Usable petrol/diesel space and operating availability need confirmation.
Investment follows the market case
Storage sizing and returns remain optional until customer access and incremental flows are evidenced. No investment conclusion is established.
15.action: Nigel: decide whether to prioritise investment after the flow case. Manish and Henry: assess inventory days, turnover, usable tanks and dispatch limits.

overview_rows:
Demand baseline and regional market
Provincial sales locate demand. Refresh the complete year and reconcile historical totals.

Domestic supply and finished imports
2024 trade is sourced, but diesel imports conflict. Match production/stocks and identify import entry ports.

Demand drivers
Vehicles, sectors, power and electrification move differently. Source the evidence first, then quantify fuel effects.

Refinery availability
Capacity has fallen. Separate operating output from conditional redevelopment and agree plant scenarios.

Competing supply routes
Compare Durban, Matola and Walvis Bay for one customer. Test full route cost, capacity and customer access.

Vopak share and additional demand
Match unique deliveries to regional demand. Test additional volumes against physical and commercial access.

Storage and optional investment
Use published tanks as context. Assess additional services only after the incremental customer-flow case.
